Rather than presenting itself as a conventional behind-the-scenes program, the special stages its information as an in-universe event. In newly shot footage, Senator Kelly, the McCarthy-like anti-mutant politician of the film, who claims to hold a list of mutants living in the United States and campaigns for a Mutant Registration Act that would force mutants to reveal their identities and abilities, addresses a Senate committee about what he describes as the growing mutant menace, while a colleague challenges his position. Intercut with the hearing, viewers learn about the making of the film through clips from the movie, rapid-fire interview excerpts with members of the cast and crew, and short glimpses behind the scenes of the production, among them the application of Rebecca Romijn-Stamos's elaborate makeup as the shape-shifting Mystique.

The special was later included as a bonus feature on some home video releases of X-Men, including Fox's DVD released on 21 November 2000, alongside an extended branching version of the film, excerpts from Charlie Rose's interview with Singer, Jackman's screen test and animatics. DVD Movie Guide described it as a glossy, promotional infomercial with a mildly clever framework, noting that its behind-the-scenes segments were brief and concluding that anyone seeking solid information about the creation of the film would have to look elsewhere.

The story begins with James Gordon Jr., the son of Commissioner James Gordon, being kidnapped by a group of thugs. Young James Jr. is taken to an abandoned warehouse where he witnesses a murder committed by a mysterious figure known as Holiday Killer. The film then jumps forward in time to show James Gordon Sr. becoming the new commissioner of Gotham City.

As Commissioner Gordon, he faces various challenges and villains, including the Riddler (Edward Nigma), who has returned to Gotham after a long absence. The Riddler is determined to prove his intellectual superiority over Batman by committing a series of murders and leaving clues for him to solve.

Meanwhile, Bruce Wayne is struggling with his own demons as he tries to balance his life as a billionaire philanthropist with his nocturnal activities as the Dark Knight. He is haunted by nightmares and struggles to connect with his parents' memory.

The story takes a dark turn when the Holiday Killer strikes again, targeting Commissioner Gordon's family. The killer is revealed to be none other than Harvey Dent, who has been driven mad by his own guilt and sense of justice.

As Batman delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the Holiday Killer is using an antique calendar as a symbol of their crimes. He also encounters the Riddler, who is determined to outsmart him at every turn.

The film ends with Batman and Harvey Dent forming an uneasy alliance to take down the Holiday Killer, but not before the killer reveals that they have one final target in mind: Commissioner Gordon's family.

Overall, Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One sets the stage for a thrilling and complex story that explores the darker side of Gotham City. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning animation, this film is sure to delight fans of the Batman franchise.

Picking up as darkness spreads across the Earth, the spirit of Sailor Saturn restores the memories of young Hotaru Tomoe, who gives Haruka, Michiru and Setsuna their crystals so that they can become Super Sailor Guardians and free their captured companions. When Zirconia mortally wounds Sailor Moon and Tuxedo Mask, Helios brings them to Elysion, the sacred realm within the Earth, where Usagi learns that the Golden Crystal, Earth's counterpart to the Silver Crystal, is sealed inside Mamoru. Meanwhile Zirconia traps Chibi Moon, Saturn and the Amazoness Quartet inside Nehelenia's mirror. Helios uses Elysion's last purifying power to save the heroes, who weaken Zirconia and break the mirror. In Elysion, a flashback reveals that Nehelenia was sealed away by Queen Serenity after cursing the newborn Princess Serenity. Nehelenia seizes the Silver Crystal, but Usagi and Mamoru's kiss breaks her nightmare; empowered by her friends and the Golden Crystal, Sailor Moon becomes Eternal Sailor Moon and destroys Nehelenia. Chibi Moon revives Helios, and the Amazoness Quartet, revealed as the asteroid Sailor Guardians, return to their slumber.

Part 2 was released in Japanese theaters on 11 February 2021, a month after the first part, which had been postponed from September 2020 by the COVID-19 pandemic; together they were the first Sailor Moon films shown in Japanese theaters in 26 years. Yasuharu Takanashi composed the score. Netflix released both parts worldwide outside Japan and mainland China on 3 June 2021. Critics were positive: Polygon praised its message of overcoming evil with love and friendship, Anime News Network gave it a B, IGN commended its stunning animation, and Den of Geek called it an enthralling adaptation. A sequel, Sailor Moon Cosmos, followed in 2023.
